stem: Aspirin belongs to which medication group and blocks substances that promote which processes?

options.label: A
options.text: Statins; only cholesterol synthesis in liver
options.misconception: Atorvastatin class — does not match the cited teaching point.
options.explanation: Wrong drug class; see the cited source passage for detail.

options.label: B
options.text: Salicylates; fever, pain, swelling, and blood clots
options.misconception: None; salicylates block mediators of fever/pain/swelling/clots.
options.explanation: MedlinePlus: salicylates block natural substances that cause fever, pain, swelling, and blood clots.

options.label: C
options.text: ACE inhibitors; only angiotensin II formation
options.misconception: Lisinopril class — does not match the cited teaching point.
options.explanation: Wrong drug class; see the cited source passage for detail.

options.label: D
options.text: Loop diuretics; only sodium reabsorption in thick ascending limb
options.misconception: Furosemide class — does not match the cited teaching point.
options.explanation: Wrong drug class; see the cited source passage for detail.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Metformin class — does not match the cited teaching point.
options.explanation: Wrong drug class; see the cited source passage for detail.

context: Learning objective: aspirin as salicylate affecting clotting mediators.
